title: Flux Architecture IR
description: Component classes + attributes + actions, generalising Accelergy's plug-in pattern beyond energy to area/leakage/latency/thermal. See docs/04.md §3.2. Amended by docs/00-decisions.md D1: covers full-SoC hierarchies (memory/compute/interconnect), not DNN-accelerator-only.

class.description: 'other' is the general-SoC escape hatch (D1) for components that aren't memory/compute/interconnect in the DNN-accelerator sense — e.g. protocol bridges, clock/power domains.

estimator_hints.description: Accelergy-style plug-in keying: which estimator plugin(s) to use for this component, generalised to any cost dimension, not just energy.

interconnect.description: System-level interconnect (NoC/D2D), distinct from per-level 'interconnect' attrs on a hierarchy entry.

noc.description: Free-form by design (existing examples use a descriptive `topology` string like 'mesh_4x4' or 'crossbar' with no further structure — see my-npu-v3.yaml, generic-riscv-soc-v1.yaml). `dimensions`, when present alongside `topology: mesh` or `topology: torus`, describes a real k-ary n-cube network (docs/00-decisions.md D5): n=2 is a 2D mesh/torus, n=3 is a real 3D NoC (die-stacked, TSV-connected layers) — same topology family, one more dimension. That specific shape maps onto evaluators/booksim's real Booksim2 integration (KNCube network, verified against real 2D and 3D simulations, not assumed); evaluators/booksim raises NotExpressibleError, not a schema error, for a `noc` block that doesn't have it — narrow validation belongs in the adapter, matching every other translator in this repo, not in this shared schema.

dimensions.description: One entry per network dimension, e.g. [8, 8] for a 2D 8x8 mesh, [4, 4, 4] for a 3D 4x4x4 mesh.

routing_function.description: Booksim2 routing function name, e.g. 'dor' (dimension-order routing).

traffic.description: Booksim2 synthetic traffic pattern name, e.g. 'uniform', 'transpose' — see evaluators/booksim/README.md for why traffic is an architecture-level (not workload-level) parameter in v0.1.

constraints.description: Machine-checkable, independent of the cost model — enforced by the validity checker even when the cost model has no opinion (anti-reward-hacking, G14).
